Article Title: Punjab opens applications for second batch of anti-drug mental health fellowship
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Reinforcing its focus on tackling substance abuse through a rehabilitation-led approach, the Punjab government launched the Leadership in Mental Health Programme (LMHP), India's first fellowship against substance abuse, in February 2026. Thirteen fellows from the inaugural cohort are currently working across Punjab to strengthen mental healthcare services and support the state's anti-drug efforts.The fellows are deployed under the Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann-led Yudh Nashean Virudh campaign, helping integrate mental healthcare and community-based rehabilitation into the state's fight against drugs. The initiative aims to strengthen rehabilitation services while placing mental health at the centre of Punjab's anti-drug strategy.The government is now preparing to launch applications for the programme's second cohort, comprising 10 fellows and seven Senior Associates, with the goal of building a statewide network of trained young professionals across all 23 districts.Implemented by the Department of Health and Family Welfare in collaboration with the state's Data Intelligence and Technical Support Unit, the programme is designed to develop mental health leaders capable of driving evidence-based prevention, treatment and rehabilitation initiatives.The fellows, selected through a rigorous process, come from diverse fields including psychology, public health and social work and commit to supporting the state's anti-drug campaign for two years.As part of the programme, they receive intensive training in psychosocial interventions, relapse prevention, programme management, community-based rehabilitation and leadership. The training is delivered with support from the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS), Mumbai, the programme's selection and knowledge partner.Health minister Balbir Singh said the fellowship seeks to combine leadership with empathy while strengthening Punjab's response to substance abuse. "Yudh Nashean Virudh is not just an initiative against drugs; it is a movement to reclaim Punjab's youth. While strict action is being taken against drug peddlers and traffickers, we are equally committed to helping every victim of drug abuse return to a life full of dignity and prevent the youth from falling into the trap of addiction. Leadership in Mental Health Programme reflects our belief that making Punjab addiction-free is possible only when enforcement, treatment, and prevention work hand-in-hand and backed by strong healthcare setup and community support," he said.The minister said addiction should be treated as a chronic health condition requiring sustained care. During their postings at district hospitals and de-addiction and rehabilitation centres, fellows work with patients and families, facilitate treatment, support relapse prevention and promote community-based rehabilitation. They also focus on reducing stigma, encouraging community participation and ensuring continuity of care after rehabilitation.Beyond district-level interventions, the first cohort is also supporting healthcare workers, strengthening service delivery and helping institutionalise best practices in Punjab's fight against substance abuse.According to the government, the programme is aimed at improving the way communities respond to substance use disorders by embedding mental health into the state's broader anti-drug campaign, with rehabilitation and long-term recovery forming a key part of the strategy.
Article Summary: The Punjab government launched the Leadership in Mental Health Programme in February 2026. The initiative aims to strengthen rehabilitation services while placing mental health at the centre of Punjab's anti-drug strategy. The fellows are deployed under the Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann's Yudh Nashean Virudh campaign.

Article Title: 'Head of family PM Modi listens': BJP's Raghav Chadha hails 'historic' anti-paper leak Bill
Article Text:
BJP MP Raghav Chadha (ANI photo)

NEW DELHI: AAP turncoat and BJP MP Raghav Chadha on Thursday broke his prolonged silence on the paper leak issue, speaking for the first time from the ruling side in Rajya Sabha. As BJP pushed the anti-paper leak Bill in the Parliament, Chadha said he did not want headlines but spoke "wholeheartedly in support of the students of India," adding that "PM Modi heard it just like the head of a family listens. "Chadha stressed that the paper leak crisis could only be resolved through an "institutional solution" and not through "media sound-bytes", which he claimed was the approach adopted by the PM Modi-led government.BJP leader said, "I don't want headline, but an outcome."Addressing NEET aspirants, he said, "Your anger is justified. Your pain is real. And your concerns about the examination system are genuine."He further said that when students raised their voices in protest, the Prime Minister listened and acted as a "guardian" to address their concerns."Students demanded, the government acted. Historic decisions taken. System changed," Chadha said.He also said that the government "heard and delivered."Highlighting the impact of paper leaks on students, he added, "Because a paper leak does not merely compromise an examination. It can wipe out years of preparation in a single moment."He further said, "Every student deserves an examination system where hard work and merit, not a leaked paper, decide the result."Months ago, Chadha led a rebel exodus from Arvind Kejriwal-founded AAP, with seven Rajya Sabha members from the party breaking away and merging their faction with the ruling BJP.However, the Bill came under sharp criticism from the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge led the attack after Union minister Jitendra Singh tabled the Bill in the Upper House.Parliament Thursday approved the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, introducing stricter penalties for paper leaks and exam-related malpractices. The government said the legislation addresses one of the biggest concerns affecting students and called for cooperation from all stakeholders to tackle the issue.The Bill was passed by a voice vote in the Rajya Sabha amid an opposition walkout, a day after it cleared the Lok Sabha.Under the amended law, individuals found guilty of paper leaks or other unfair means in public examinations will face a minimum prison term of five years, extendable to 10 years, along with a fine of up to Rs 50 lakh.For organised exam-related crimes, the Bill prescribes a minimum jail term of seven years and a fine of up to Rs 10 crore.The legislation also empowers state governments and Union Territory administrations to designate Courts of Session as special fast-track courts to try offences under the Act. These courts will conduct day-to-day proceedings and complete trials within three months of the filing of the chargesheet.The Bill further authorises the central government to constitute a special task force to investigate offences under the Act whenever necessary.
Article Summary: BJP leader said, "I don't want headline, but an outcome" Chadha led a rebel exodus from Arvind Kejriwal-founded AAP, with seven Rajya Sabha members from the party breaking away and merging their faction with the ruling BJP.

The Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA) has released the NEET UG 2026 score list for 69,170 qualified candidates who selected Karnataka as their state in the National Testing Agency (NTA) application form. The list has been published on the official KEA website in descending order of merit and will be used as a reference document for the upcoming Karnataka medical counselling process.The official announcement was issued by KEA Executive Director H. Prasanna, IAS. The published score list includes candidates eligible for consideration under Karnataka state counselling based on their NEET UG 2026 performance. The candidate securing the All India 20th rank has topped the Karnataka state merit list.NEET UG 2026 Karnataka score list detailsThe KEA score list has been prepared based on NEET UG 2026 scores of candidates who mentioned Karnataka in their NTA application. The document is available in PDF format on the official KEA portal.Candidates can access the score list by visiting the KEA website and opening the UGNEET-2026 section under the latest announcements. The PDF can be searched using the candidate's NEET roll number, name or application number.The merit list is provisional and has been released for the purpose of Karnataka state-level counselling for undergraduate medical and dental admissions.Candidates can follow these steps to download the Karnataka NEET UG 2026 score list:Step 1: Visit the official KEA website.Step 2: Open the UGNEET-2026 or NEET UG 2026 section.Step 3: Click on the score list or merit list PDF link.Step 4: Download the document.Step 5: Use the search option to find the NEET roll number, name or application number.Candidates should save a copy of the score list for future counselling-related requirements.KEA has not yet released the complete round-wise schedule for Karnataka NEET UG 2026 counselling. Further rounds, including Round 2 and the Mop-Up round, are expected to continue in September 2026.Candidates applying for All India Quota seats must participate separately through the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) counselling process.Candidates should keep their NEET UG roll number, application details and required admission documents ready for upcoming counselling activities. They are advised to regularly check the official KEA website for the detailed information bulletin and updated schedule.The score list will help candidates understand their Karnataka merit position before the commencement of seat allotment activities.

Article Title: Who is Seema Kaliramna? The mother and PhD scholar who won Commonwealth Games 2026 bronze

Who is Seema Kaliramna ?

NEW DELHI: Indian discus thrower Seema Kaliramna won bronze medal in the women's discus throw at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow. She secured third place with a best throw of 58.65m.Seema had only two valid throws in six attempts. After starting with a foul, Seema reached 57.32m and then threw to 58.65 before ending her campaign with three foul throws. But the 58.65m was enough to earn her a bronze medal.Jamaica's Samantha Hall claimed the gold medal with a Games-leading throw of 61.66m, while Canada's Julia Tunks won silver with 60.67m.Seema is one of India's top discus throwers from Haryana. Along with being an athlete, she is also pursuing a PhD in Physical Education at Chaudhary Bansi Lal University (CBLU) in Bhiwani.Her father, a former basketball player and javelin thrower in the Indian Army, introduced her to sports at a young age.Today, she is coached by her husband, Ravinder Kaliramna, popularly known as Monu Kaliramna, who is a former national-level discus thrower.After the birth of her son, Rudra, Seema took a break from athletics.However, she made an inspiring comeback just 11 months later, balancing training, motherhood and her PhD studies.She won the gold medal at the 2025 National Games and later claimed the national title. At the National Inter-State Senior Athletics Championships in Bhubaneswar, she produced a personal best throw of 59.73m to qualify for the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.Seema has represented India at several international events, including the Youth Asian Championships. She also won gold at the first Khelo India University Games in 2020.Seema credited her husband and coach Ravinder for her CWG success."I am very happy. This was my first Commonwealth Games, and winning a bronze medal makes it even more special. I did not face any major difficulties during the competition. The only challenge was the cold weather, because I had to keep warming up repeatedly. Overall, it was a very good competition," Seema said."My husband arrived just two days ago. He [her son] was telling me to take him along, but this is a very emotional moment. My situation is such that I cannot bring my son with me. It is extremely difficult and painful. You can call it a sacrifice," she said."AFI has supported me tremendously, and SAI has also played a big role in my journey. Whenever I needed anything else, my family was always there to support me. I would like to dedicate this medal to my husband. All the hard work and sacrifices behind this achievement have been possible because of his constant support," Seema said.
Article Summary: Seema Kaliramna won bronze medal in the women's discus throw at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow. She secured third place with a best throw of 58.65m. Seema credited her husband and coach Ravinder for her CWG success.

Article Title: After made-in-India bullet train, new high-speed corridors to get indigenous signalling system
Article Text:
India will develop its own control protocols for high-speed rail.

India’s indigenous signalling system for bullet trains

7 High-Speed Rail Corridors Planned

India is aiming to achieve new milestones in manufacturing with its first bullet train project. After deciding to manufacture the high-speed train indigenously for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor, Indian Railways is now looking at in-house advanced signalling system for other upcoming corridors.Indian Railways is developing an indigenous signalling protocol for high-speed rail called the Bharat Train Control System (BTCS). The system is being designed specifically for Indian operating conditions and aims to eliminate dependence on foreign signalling protocols for the nearly 7,000 km of new bullet train corridors planned across the country.Earlier this month, former Japanese minister Hideki Makihara criticised India for not exclusively adopting Japanese technology for the MAHSR project, pointing to its decision to use open-source signalling protocols instead of Japan's Digital Automatic Train Control system.Responding to these concerns, officials said trains supplied by Japan's Hitachi are compatible with ETCS, but added that "offers from them (Japan) need to come first".Also Read | Why India making its own bullet trains is a big deal - explained The official further said India is also "open to allowing switchover to Japanese protocols once suppliers place appropriate proposals".Officials told ET that approvals for the designs and route alignments of future high-speed rail corridors are expected to be completed by mid-2027."India will develop its own control protocols for high-speed rail," a senior official told the financial daily, adding that the new system will build on the experience gained from the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (MAHSR) corridor, where the European Train Control System (ETCS) is currently being deployed."The Bharat Train Control System will be open-source, cost-effective and can be tailored to requirements of rapid and safe deployment across the country," the official said, adding that once developed, the technology could also be offered to other countries.The official added that introducing an indigenous high-speed rail signalling protocol would provide a significant boost to domestic railway design companies and equipment manufacturers.In June last year, the National High Speed Rail Corporation Ltd (NHSRCL) awarded a Rs 4,100 crore contract for the signalling system on the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (MAHSR) corridor to a consortium comprising India's Dineshchandra R Agrawal Infracon Pvt Ltd and Germany's Siemens.The consortium is deploying an ETCS Level 2-based signalling system capable of supporting train operations at speeds of up to 350 kmph.The Delhi-Meerut Rapid Rail Corridor, which currently operates India's fastest train, is also equipped with ETCS Level 2 signalling, supplied and implemented by France's Alstom.According to industry observers, the decision to adopt ETCS Level 2 for the Japan-backed MAHSR project enabled a broader pool of equipment suppliers to participate.
Article Summary: Indian Railways is developing an indigenous signalling protocol for high-speed rail. The Bharat Train Control System (BTCS) is being designed specifically for Indian operating conditions. The system aims to eliminate dependence on foreign signalling protocols for the nearly 7,000 km of new bullet train corridors.

Article Title: ‘Unlucky’ taunts, dowry demands: Dehradun teacher dies, husband, in-laws booked
Article Text: DEHRADUN: A case has been registered against a personal secretary at the Uttarakhand Secretariat and his family members for allegedly causing the dowry death of his 27-year-old wife, Shristi Bhandari, a government school teacher, in Dehradun's Doiwala area.Acting on a complaint filed by the victim's mother, Seema Bhandari, police on Thursday registered an FIR under Section 80(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with dowry death, against Shristi's husband, Saurabh Khatri, his mother Parvina Devi, sister Charu Khatri and other unidentified family members.According to the complaint, Shristi married Khatri in November last year and lived with his family in Doiwala, around 20 km from Dehradun. Soon after the marriage, her husband and in-laws allegedly began subjecting her to physical and mental cruelty while demanding dowry.Circle Officer (Doiwala) Vandana Verma said the family regularly humiliated Shristi by calling her "inauspicious" and "unlucky"."They socially humiliated her, claiming that misfortunes began after her arrival. When her father-in-law passed away after a prolonged illness, the family blamed her for his death as well," CO Verma said.The incident came to light after Seema Bhandari was unable to contact her daughter on July 28 and 29 and asked relatives living nearby to check on her. They found Shristi in a critical condition at a local hospital. By the time her mother reached Dehradun from Srinagar in Garhwal, Shristi had died during treatment.
Article Summary: Shristi Bhandari, 27, a government school teacher, died in Dehradun's Doiwala area. Her husband and in-laws allegedly began subjecting her to physical and mental cruelty while demanding dowry. The family regularly humiliated Shristi by calling her "inauspicious" and "unlucky"

NEW DELHI: Underscoring the need for an independent and impartial process for selection of the chief election commissioner and election commissioners, Supreme Court on Thursday said Election Commission must not only act independently but must also be seen to act independently. The court questioned why Parliament, while framing the law, decided not to include Chief Justice of India in the selection panel.A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma said the CJI was part of selection panels for CBI director and Lokpal, and asked what could be the reason for excluding him from the process of selecting CEC and ECs — posts that are among the most important for a democracy. The court reserved its verdict on the Centre’s plea that the matter be referred to a constitution bench.The court is hearing challenges to the constitutional validity of the 2023 Act, under which CEC and ECs are appointed by President on the recommendation of a selection committee consisting of PM, leader of the opposition, and a Union Cabinet minister nominated by PM. SG Tushar Mehta argued that the court could not begin with an assumption that the PM would act against democratic principles.In 2023, a five-judge constitution bench of SC had directed that pending enactment of a law by Parliament, appointments should be made by a panel comprising the PM, CJI and leader of the opposition to infuse independence into the process. Parliament subsequently enacted the 2023 Act, which replaced the CJI with a cabinet minister.Attorney general (AG) R Venkataramani and solicitor general (SG) Tushar Mehta urged the bench not to question the wisdom of Parliament, arguing that doing so would amount to interference with the independence of the legislature. The AG said Parliament’s legislative choice could not be questioned merely because another model was possible, and that “Parliament cannot be gagged”. The SG added that the three organs of the state — executive, legislature and judiciary — were independent, and their independence must be respected.“People must trust the Prime Minister. The office of the Prime Minister has a sanctity attached… If his decision is not to be trusted and is to be seen as necessarily a bad-faith exercise, then why not have a provision that even while selecting his cabinet he must consult some former judge or outsider?” SG Mehta said.Mehta added that one organ of the state could not proceed on the basis that the PM and other ministers would act in bad faith or against constitutional principles simply because they have the numerical majority.The bench clarified that there was no question of not trusting the PM. However, it asked the SG how many ministers in the government had cases pending against them, recalling that the court had earlier reposed trust in the elected government to ensure that people with criminal antecedents were not appointed as ministers.“It is not a lack of faith. The election commissioner has to be an independent person. Should there not be a show of fairness? We are not saying fairness has not been achieved by this committee. Just like justice is not only to be done, it has to be shown to be done, we are on the second part,” the bench said.Government requested that the petitions be referred to a larger constitution bench, arguing that an important question of law was involved. This plea was strongly opposed by senior advocates D Seshadri Naidu, Gopal Sankaranarayanan, Prashant Bhushan and Sanjay Parikh, who contended that government was raising this ground after 20 days of hearing and should not be allowed to do so.In an affidavit, government countered the petitioners’ claim that the independence of Election Commission would be compromised by replacing CJI with a cabinet minister. It maintained that there was no flaw in the law passed by Parliament, and that free and fair elections had never been casualties even when appointments were made solely by the executive for over seven decades.Government described as hypothetical the suggestion that vesting the executive with exclusive authority in EC appointments would necessarily compromise the independence of the poll watchdog.
Article Summary: Supreme Court says Election Commission must not only act independently but must also be seen to act independently. Court questions why Parliament decided not to include Chief Justice of India in the selection panel. Court is hearing challenges to the constitutional validity of the 2023 Act.

Article Title: ‘Normal’ July rain defies forecast of El Nino impact
Article Text:
Monsoon in India (representative image)

El Niño alone can no more explain India’s rain pattern: Experts

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s monsoon has delivered a surprise this July, defying forecasts of below-normal rainfall despite a strengthening El Nino and reinforcing scientists’ warnings that climate change is altering the country’s most important weather system, report Chittaranjan Tembhekar & Gaurav Talwar.As of July 30, India received 270.1mm of rains in July against a normal of 271.9mm, well within normal range. IMD had said July rainfall was likely to be less than 94% of long period average.However, rainfall distribution remained skewed, with central India receiving 29% excess in July while the east & northeast recorded a deficit of 30% and south 28%.The monsoon deficit since June 1 was 14%. The unexpected turnaround in July has eased fears of a big monsoon shortfall but highlighted a new reality: long dry spells interspersed with short bursts of extremely heavy rain capable of triggering floods and landslides.According to a Climate Trends briefing, successive weather systems cut the national rainfall deficit considerably from 40% at the end of June.Scientists say the biggest lesson from monsoon 2026 is that El Niño alone can no longer explain India’s rainfall behaviour.Global warming, warming oceans and changing atmospheric circulation are increasingly interacting with traditional climate drivers, making monsoon forecasts more difficult.“The challenge is no longer predicting how much rain India will receive, but forecasting where, when and how intensely it will fall in a warming climate,” scientists said.Rainfall remained highly uneven. While 16 meteorological subdivisions states recorded normal rainfall in the season and three saw excess to large-excess rainfall, 17 subdivisions remained deficient. Central India was almost normal with a 1% surplus, northwest India had an 11% shortfall, while east and northeast India remained 30% below normal and south India 25% deficient.The findings are particularly striking because the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration has projected an 81% probability of a very strong El Niño developing between Oct and Dec — a pattern usually associated with weaker Indian monsoons.Former IMD director general K J Ramesh attributed July’s recovery to abnormal warming over the western Pacific, which spawned successive monsoon systems over the Bay of Bengal, and the increasing influence of Western Disturbances that enhanced rainfall over Maharashtra and Gujarat.“Climate change is reshaping the characteristics of the monsoon, which existing models are failing to take into account,” Ramesh said.Akshay Deoras of the University of Reading said the monsoon rebounded rapidly after an early July lull. He cited Umbergaon in Gujarat receiving 1,064 mm of rain in 24 hours —among the highest daily totals recorded since 1901 — as evidence of intensifying rainfall extremes, adding that climate change appears to be amplifying the monsoon’s internal weather systems.
Article Summary: India received 270.1mm of rains in July against a normal of 271.9mm, well within normal range. But rainfall distribution remained skewed, with central India receiving 29% excess in July while the east & northeast recorded a deficit of 30% and south 28%.

Article Title: Anti-paper leak bill clears Parliament; PM Modi says it will build a credible exam system

NEW DELHI: Parliament on Thursday approved a bill to amend the anti-paper leak law, prescribing stricter punishment, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi saying an important step towards building a credible exam system has been taken.In a selfie-video message, the Prime Minister asserted that gangs behind exam paper leaks, which play with the future of students, will not be spared, and stringent laws are needed to deal with them. "Our work will continue and we will not allow this situation to persist for long," he said.For the past many decades every state govt and the Centre have faced this menace of paper leaks, which is posing a crisis for students, the PM said about the bill that proposes a longer jail term and steeper fine. "It has become necessary to bring reforms in the education system in all states and at the Centre," Modi said, asking the youth to work together with govt to fulfil the dream of a developed India.His government, he said, has taken a series of steps for reforming the exam system, be it forming a task force, constituting fast-track courts or taking into consideration the views of states. Optimal use of technology is necessary, he added.Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, was cleared by voice vote in RS amid a walkout by a large section of the opposition, a day after it was passed by LS. This will become a law after the President's assent.Replying to the discussion on the bill in Rajya Sabha, Union minister Jitendra Singh highlighted measures taken by govt in the education sector, including NEP-2020 and an increase in the number of universities.Earlier in the day, Singh had told the Upper House that the bill testifies the govt does not stand on prestige and is open to healthy inputs. "We are open to constructive suggestions from all quarters, and that's exactly the reason why, in the wake of the recent sequence of events, the PM lost no time to declare that nobody will be allowed to jeopardise the future of our children and also announced the resolve of zero tolerance to paper leaks," he said.According to the bill, individuals involved in paper leaks or unfair means in exams will get jail terms for a minimum of five years and a maximum of 10 years and a fine of up to Rs 50 lakh. For organised crimes, it proposes a minimum sentence of seven years and a fine of up to Rs 10 crore. The bill also seeks to empower all state govts and UT administrations to designate any court of session as a special fast-track court to try offences under the proposed law.The bill also empowers the central govt to constitute a special task force for the investigation of any offence, if necessary.
Article Summary: Rajya Sabha clears it by voice vote amid opposition’s walkout. PM Narendra Modi says it is an important step towards building a credible exam system. The bill proposes a longer jail term and steeper fine. It will become a law after President's assent.

BENGALURU: The department of space (DoS) and Isro have launched one of their widest recruitment drives in recent years, announcing 746 openings across scientists, administrative staff and apprentices over the past week, at least 43 of which are against “backlog vacancies”.The recruitment, spread across three notifications issued between July 27 and July 29, covers 336 regular posts and 410 apprenticeship positions, reflecting an effort to strengthen both the organisation’s immediate workforce and its future talent pipeline.TOI highlighted on July 18 how DoS was battling a 25-year-high vacancy rate with nearly three out of every 10 sanctioned posts lying unfilled at the end of 2025-26 — staffing had fallen to 72.2%, the lowest level in at least 25 years.The largest chunk of the latest recruitment drive is to fill up 244 Level-4 administrative posts through the Isro Centralised Recruitment Board (ICRB). These include 113 assistants, 81 junior personal assistants, 22 upper division clerks, 10 stenographers, 17 assistants for autonomous institutions and one junior personal assistant for an autonomous institution.The recruitment also includes 92 scientist/engineer ‘SC’ posts in level-10 of the pay matrix.Electronics accounts for the largest share with 34 vacancies, followed by mechanical (26), computer science (13), civil (10), electrical (4), refrigeration & air-conditioning (2), architecture (2) and one civil engineer post at the Physical Research Laboratory (PRL), Ahmedabad.Unlike the administrative recruitment, these scientists will be deployed across specialised centres depending on discipline. The notification lists URSC and Human Space Flight Centre (HSFC), Bengaluru; VSSC, Thiruvananthapuram — two of the centres that have seen most attrition in recent years — Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota; SAC, Ahmedabad; NRSC, Hyderabad; LPSC, Valiamala; Isro Propulsion Complex (IPRC), Mahendragiri; Istrac and Isro headquarters in Bengaluru.Alongside permanent recruitment, URSC, Bengaluru, has announced 410 apprenticeship positions for 2026-27. These comprise 220 graduate apprentices, 120 technician apprentices and 70 diploma in commercial practice apprentices.Graduate apprenticeship intake is dominated by electronics and communication engineering (83 positions), followed by mechanical (50), computer science (40), chemical (15), industrial engineering and management (10), aeronautical (10), aerospace (10) and automobile engineering (2). Technician apprenticeships include 38 electronics, 30 computer science, 30 mechanical, 10 electrical, 5 civil, 5 instrumentation and 2 automobile engineering positions.It is noteworthy that Isro hires apprentices to fulfill statutory requirements under the Apprentices Act, 1961, and train fresh graduates. While candidates receive a monthly stipend — for the current positions it is Rs 10,900 for one category and Rs 12,300 for the other — and a certificate and a monthly stipend, but no permanent job is guaranteed.The latest recruitment is unlikely to substantially alter DoS’ staffing profile in the immediate future. Even after excluding apprenticeship positions, the 336 regular vacancies now advertised amount to less than 6% of the department's existing 5,632 vacancies documented earlier this year.Sources in Isro told TOI that the agency had called for some positions, including for junior research fellows, project associates, research associates, technical and scientific assistants aside from 44 apprentices across North Eastern Space Applications Centre (NESAC), URSC, Istract and SDSC between June and early July.
Article Summary: The recruitment, spread across three notifications issued between July 27 and July 29, covers 336 regular posts and 410 apprenticeship positions. NEW DELHI: More than 11 years after a Delhi court sensationally summoned former PM Manmohan Singh as an accused in a coal block allotment scam case, the Supreme Court Wednesday gave him a clean chit, closing the case nearly two years after his demise.Special judge Bharat Parashar, presiding over trials in coal block allotment scam cases which were investigated by the CBI under the SC’s monitoring, had on March 11, 2015, issued summons to Singh in the case relating to irregular allocation of Talabira-II coal block in Odisha to Kumar Mangalam Birla-owned Hindalco. Singh held the charge of coal ministry at the time of the allocation in question.Parashar, now the secretary general of SC, had declined to close the cases despite the CBI filing two successive reports — on Aug 27, 2014, and Oct 21, 2014 — recommending the same.Since the Supreme Court had barred Delhi HC from entertaining appeals against interim orders of the special judge, Singh moved SC challenging trial court’s order.A bench of Justices V Gopala Gowda and C Nagappan had on April 1, 2015, stayed the summoning order, saving the ex-PM the embarrassment of appearing as an accused in the Patiala House Court complex.On Wednesday, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, who had earlier successfully argued in SC for staying the proceedings against Singh, told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalaya Bagchi and V Mohana that though the proceedings would abate due to Singh’s demise in Nov 2024, the court should remove the trial court’s observations against the ex-PM in the summoning order.Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi joined Sibal to reiterate the request.Both the special public prosecutor and senior advocate R S Cheema and additional solicitor general S V Raju had recused themselves, leaving the court with the task of perusing the CBI closure reports on its own before passing the order.The CJI-led bench said the demise of an accused would ordinarily result in the abatement of case against him. After perusing the closure reports, it allowed Singh’s appeal and quashed the trial court’s order taking cognisance of the crime and issuing summons to Singh.
Article Summary: A Delhi court sensationally summoned former PM Manmohan Singh as an accused in a coal block allotment scam case. The Supreme Court Wednesday gave him a clean chit, closing the case nearly two years after his demise. Singh held the charge of coal ministry at the time of the allocation in question.

NEW DELHI: Over 200 academicians have written an open letter objecting to Priyanka Gandhi Vadra 's 'gaumutra' expert jibe at IIT Madras director V Kamakoti and said dismissing a scholar through a label risks undermining the scientific temper promoted by the Constitution.The first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, is credited with popularising the term 'scientific temper', and the 215 academicians have invoked it to criticise Priyanka, saying scientists, scholars and educators deserve to know that they can participate in public debate without fear of being reduced to dismissive labels.They defended Kamakoti's advocacy of cow urine, which is traditionally associated with some therapeutic benefits, and said scientific temper is not merely scepticism towards unconventional ideas but also the willingness to examine claims objectively before accepting or rejecting them. NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday directed Delhi government to provide treatment to those injured during students’ protests but found a plea for ban on use of pellet guns for crowd control vague and asked when police are permitted to fire bullets in extreme situations, how could pellet guns be banned.Appearing for petitioners, advocate Vrinda Grover questioned the legality of Rapid Action Force using pellet guns against student protesters on July 20 at Jantar Mantar, and urged the SC to direct the Union govt to preserve the ammunition log of RAF during their deployment at the protest site and award exemplary compensation to those injured by metallic pellets.The petition was filed by Sheikh Irshad Mansoori and Prashant Kumar Singh, who suffered injuries from pellet guns on July 20, and former IPS officer Yashovardhan Azad.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana directed preservation of the logbook, and solicitor general Tushar Mehta said all documents required for an effective investigation into alleged police excesses and violence at the protest site would be preserved.When Grover persisted with the plea for a ban on use of pellet guns, Justice Bagchi termed the prayer vague and said, “Police regulations permit use of pellet guns in exceptional circumstances.If you want phasing out of pellet guns, then you must challenge those regulations, which you have not done.“You say at no stage metallic pellet can be used, when graded response permits use of bullets in extreme situations. Seeking ban on use of pellet guns cannot be on the same plane as seeking a ban on use of bullets (for crowd dispersal)? Law permits use of bullets.”Justice Bagchi recalled a Calcutta High Court order quashing a colonial-era police regulation asking personnel to fire at chests instead of legs of protesters to save ammunition.The bench said Azad needed to amend the relief sought in his petition as there could be an SOP for police’s graded action delineating when to use rubber pellets followed by metallic pellets. Grover agreed to amend the prayer to enable the SC to provide guidelines for the police’s crowd dispersal action.The bench reiterated that there were occasions when peaceful protests were hijacked by miscreants and became vehicles for ulterior purposes, including for the purpose of sabotaging the bona fide aim of the protests.“All such situations would require various graded responses. But most important is to equip police with adequate safety gear. Only then can they ponder over graded responses to violent crowds. Otherwise, the protesters and police, both are human beings and react equally to threats coming to them,” the bench said. The SG said citizens always have a right to non-violent protest.Grover said updated guidelines framed by Bureau of Police Research and Development (BPRD) were not available after 2016 and it was very difficult to obtain information from police. The bench said this was not correct and such guidelines should be uploaded on websites. The SG said he would check the veracity of Azad’s allegation.The SC had said on July 28 that it was prima facie convinced about a high-level inquiry into alleged police excesses and violence against cops and directed police to preserve data collected from various cameras but restrained them from taking coercive action against students and making public their personal data.Grover said petitioners Mansoori and Singh were injured by metallic pellets fired by RAF without provocation. She said while Mansoori received good treatment at Lady Hardinge Hospital, Singh did not, leading the SC to direct Delhi govt to provide adequate treatment to the two and all those injured during the protests led by CJP.
Article Summary: The petition was filed by Sheikh Irshad Mansoori and Prashant Kumar Singh, who suffered injuries from pellet guns on July 20. The bench said Azad needed to amend the relief sought in his petition as there could be an SOP for police’s graded action.

Article Title: India's solar problem isn't generation anymore. It's what to do with all that power
Article Text:
From solar laggard to powerhouse

The paradox

Why more solar can stress the grid

What is driving it

The grid is changing fast

Will the boom continue?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The next chapter

For decades, India’s energy challenge could be simply summed up: build more capacity. More coal, more transmission lines, more renewable energy. Solar, in particular, became the poster child of the country’s clean energy ambitions.Now, success has created a new problem.Across India’s vast solar parks, electricity is increasingly generated faster than the grid can absorb it. Panels continue to harvest abundant sunshine, but not every electron finds a home.It is an irony few would have predicted a decade ago.India’s solar revolution is no longer constrained primarily by a lack of generation capacity. It is increasingly constrained by the ability to move, store and use the electricity it produces.That paradox, producing too much clean electricity at the wrong time, could define the next phase of India’s energy transition.India’s solar story has been one of the country’s most remarkable infrastructure transformations.India gets 250–300 sunny days a year in most parts of the country, with solar insolation of 4–7 kWh per square metre per day. A recent working paper by the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM) says India’s installed solar capacity has expanded from just 3 GW in 2014 to around 157 GW by May 2026.Solar has emerged as the largest contributor within India’s renewable energy portfolio, overtaking other clean energy sources in installed capacity, according to the Press Information Bureau (PIB).The country now ranks third globally in installed solar capacity, according to the Renewable Energy Statistics 2026, reflecting how rapidly India has scaled deployment.This growth has helped transform India’s wider electricity system.As of October 2025, non-fossil fuel sources accounted for more than half of India’s installed electricity capacity, another milestone highlighted by the PIB.The expansion also underpins India’s Panchamrit commitments announced at COP26, including achieving 500 GW of non-fossil electricity capacity by 2030 and ultimately reaching net-zero emissions by 2070.Yet the country’s greatest solar success has also exposed its weakest link.The warning signs are becoming increasingly difficult to ignore.According to a written reply in Parliament by minister of state for Renewable Energy Shripad Yesso Naik , India curtailed 8,133 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of solar electricity during the April–June period because the grid could not absorb all the renewable power being generated.The curtailment rose from 2,417 GWh in April to 3,235 GWh in May before easing slightly to 2,481 GWh in June, according to government data reported by Reuters.The government attributed the restrictions to grid security requirements and a mismatch between renewable energy projects coming online ahead of the transmission infrastructure needed to evacuate that power.In effect, India is generating clean electricity that cannot always be delivered to consumers.The problem is not confined to isolated projects. Government data also show that around 21 GW of renewable energy capacity is currently connected through temporary transmission arrangements, while another 12 GW cannot inject full power into the grid because of transmission constraints.At first glance, the situation seems counterintuitive.How can a country simultaneously require more renewable energy while asking existing solar plants to reduce output?The answer lies in how electricity systems function.Solar generation peaks around midday, when sunshine is strongest.Electricity demand, however, often reaches its highest point after sunset, precisely when solar output begins to fall.The result is a widening mismatch between when electricity is generated and when it is most needed.The EAC-PM working paper argues that India’s electricity challenge has fundamentally changed. “The active constraint for the grid has shifted from generation capacity to flexibility,” the report says.The paper describes India’s increasingly pronounced “duck curve,” a phenomenon seen in many high-renewable electricity systems where solar generation creates a deep trough in daytime demand from conventional power plants, followed by a steep evening surge once the sun sets.The transformation has been rapid.Between May 2023 and May 2026, the evening net-load ramp nearly doubled, from about 36 GW to 74 GW, while the morning decline as solar flooded the grid almost tripled, from 18 GW to 53 GW, according to the EAC-PM analysis.The surge has been driven by a combination of ambitious policy support and falling solar costs.Government flagship programmes such as PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana aim to install rooftop solar systems in one crore households. By December 2025, 23.9 lakh households had already installed rooftop systems with around 7 GW of capacity, while more than Rs 13,464 crore had been released as subsidies, according to the PIB.Meanwhile, the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for high-efficiency solar PV modules, with a total outlay of Rs 24,000 crore, seeks to build domestic manufacturing capacity and reduce import dependence.India has also accelerated utility-scale solar parks and expanded renewable procurement through competitive bidding.The result has been unprecedented capacity addition. According to NITI Aayog’s India Climate and Energy Dashboard, renewable energy capacity increased from 58 GW in 2020–21 to around 283 GW by May 2026, with solar alone contributing approximately 157 GW.Electricity demand itself is rising at remarkable speed.According to the Central Electricity Authority (CEA), peak demand increased from 190 GW in 2020–21 to around 250 GW in 2024–25, while annual electricity requirement rose from 1,276 billion units to 1,694 billion units over the same period.The trend has continued.On May 21, 2026, India’s grid recorded its highest-ever demand, touching 270.8 GW, according to the EAC-PM.Yet that same day revealed another striking reality.Electricity traded on the Indian Energy Exchange cleared at just Rs 1.56 per unit at 1 pm, when solar generation flooded the grid. By 6.30 pm, after sunset, prices had surged to the market ceiling of Rs 10 per unit.India is not short of electricity during the day. It is short of flexibility after dark.Another hurdle lies in India’s domestic manufacturing ecosystem. Even as the government pushes for self-reliance in solar equipment, manufacturers are struggling with shortages of locally made solar cells.According to Reuters, nearly one-third of India’s small and medium-sized solar module manufacturers have halted production, while others have cut operating days because of waiting periods of up to eight months for domestic cells. With India still relying on China for around 95% of its solar cell imports, the supply crunch threatens to slow capacity expansion and raise production costs, exposing the gap between policy ambition and manufacturing readiness.Almost certainly.India’s clean energy targets remain among the world’s most ambitious, and policy momentum shows little sign of slowing. The challenge, however, is shifting from building generation assets to building an electricity system capable of handling them.Flattening even half of a typical summer evening demand ramp would require around 130 GWh of battery discharge, far exceeding India’s present storage capability.While pumped hydro projects have advanced steadily, battery deployment remains well behind projections. Recent additions have raised battery energy storage capacity to around 2.7 GW, but a substantial gap remains.Recognising this, proposed amendments to the Electricity Act and consumer rules seek to formally integrate energy storage into India’s power system, deepen electricity markets, strengthen non-fossil obligations and accelerate time-of-day tariffs, all intended to improve grid flexibility.India’s solar journey is, in many ways, a victim of its own success.The next decade of India’s energy transition will be defined less by the number of panels installed than by the intelligence of the grid behind them. Transmission lines, batteries, storage technologies, flexible markets and smarter demand management will determine whether India’s abundant sunshine translates into reliable clean power.
Article Summary: Solar has emerged as the largest contributor within India’s renewable energy portfolio, overtaking other clean energy sources in installed capacity. The country now ranks third globally in installed solar capacity, according to the Renewable Energy Statistics 2026. Between May 2023 and May 2026, the net-load solar capacity nearly doubled, from about 36 GW to 74 GW.

JAMMU: J&K Police attached properties of five Pakistan-based terrorist handlers in Reasi district on Thursday to prevent their misuse for terror financing in the Union Territory.The attachment — linked to a case registered at Mahore PS under the provisions of BNS, Unlawful Activities Prevention Act, and Egress and Internal Movement Control Ordinance Act — was carried out by a police team led by Mahore SDPO Parul Bhardwaj in the presence of the executive magistrate and local witnesses, a spokesperson said.The land belonged to Alaf Din (7 kanals), Ghulam Mohammad (10 kanals and 11 marlas), Mohammed Asraf (17 marlas), Shabir Ahmad (7 kanals and 3 marlas), and Bahar Din (8 kanals and 1 marla). NEW DELHI: Amid the deepening Middle East crisis, PM Narendra Modi Thursday chaired what was the fourth special meeting of the cabinet committee on security (CCS) and directed establishment of a mechanism to provide timely information, emergency assistance and counselling to seafarers, serving on both domestic and foreign-flagged vessels, and their families."The PM said all efforts must be made to safeguard citizens as well as the Indian diaspora from the impact of this conflict," an official statement said. It added that Modi also addressed issues related to fertilisers, energy and safety of Indian diaspora and seafarers, while calling for a whole-of-government approach to tackle the challenges.The release said the meeting also assessed the fertiliser requirement for the ensuing rabi season and discussed alternative sources of fertilisers. "PM said that all measures be taken for ensuring uninterrupted supply of fertilisers," it said.Persons familiar with the discussion said fertiliser stock was 30-35% higher than last year and there was no reason for any concern.Similarly, in the case of gas as well as crude oil, supplies were more than adequate, with cabinet secretary T V Somanathan in a presentation underlining that government’s strategy to diversify the sources had helped mitigate the risk.“Availability of adequate crude oil has enabled central public sector enterprise refineries to operate at utilisation levels exceeding 100%, ensuring continued production of petrol, diesel and other petroleum products. Initiatives have also been taken to expand PNG connections which have resulted in substantial increase in PNG connections,” it said.Besides, it said, government was also facilitating industrial substitution of LPG through expansion of the National Gas Grid, augmentation of LNG import and regasification infrastructure, expansion of city gas distribution networks, faster approvals for expansion of the pipeline infrastructure.PM stressed to ensure energy independence, emphasis should be made on renewable energy sources, including solar energy and other non-fossil-fuel based sources. The meeting took place amid escalation on multiple fronts in the Middle East region, including fresh US-Iran strikes and maritime and energy disruptions.“PM said a whole of government approach be continued to be adopted to tackle the challenges arising due to the crisis. He said that a unified coordinated mechanism be put in place for regular monitoring of all the developments to ensure expeditious implementation of appropriate measures to safeguard the interests of the citizens.”
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi chaired fourth special meeting of the cabinet committee on security. He directed establishment of a mechanism to provide timely information, emergency assistance and counselling to seafarers, serving on both domestic and foreign-flagged vessels. Modi also addressed issues related to fertilisers, energy and safety of Indian diaspora and seafarers.

SRINAGAR: J&K government approved Thursday Rs 41.16 lakh for a gas agency promised to pellet survivor Insha Mushtaq eight years ago, reviving a rehabilitation pledge that had remained frozen since the fall of PDP-BJP govt in 2018.The approval marks a turning point for Insha from Sedow village of Shopian, who lost her eyesight at 14 after a pellet gun struck her on July 12, 2016, during protests following Hizbul Mujahideen commander Burhan Wani’s killing.“Justice delayed but not denied,” minister for food, civil supplies and consumer affairs Satish Sharma posted on X after the approval.The gas agency was announced by then CM Mehbooba Mufti after meeting Insha during her treatment.Doctors said pellets ruptured her right eye, badly damaged her left eye and fractured her nasal, frontal and maxillary bones. Article Title: Calling registered AYUSH doctors 'quacks' has no legal basis: NCISM
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a move likely to intensify the debate over the status of traditional medicine practitioners, the National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM) has warned that calling duly registered AYUSH doctors "quacks" or "bogus doctors" has no legal basis and could violate their legal and constitutional rights.The commission said it had come to its notice that qualified practitioners holding recognised degrees in Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha and Sowa-Rigpa were being subjected to harassment, defamation and false characterisation through public notices, print and electronic media, social media platforms and other public forums.The NCISM said practitioners registered with the appropriate State Medical Councils for Indian Medicine and recognised under the Indian Medicine Central Council Act, 1970, and the NCISM Act, 2020, are legally recognised medical practitioners. It said the NCISM Act provides the statutory framework for regulating education, ethics and professional practice in Indian systems of medicine and confers legal rights and responsibilities on registered practitioners."There is no legal basis for describing such registered practitioners as 'quacks' or 'bogus doctors'," the commission said, adding that any individual, institution, media organisation or authority publicly using such terms may be acting contrary to the legal recognition granted under the NCISM Act, 2020, and may be infringing upon the practitioners' professional and constitutional rights.Reiterating its position, the commission said all duly qualified and registered practitioners of the Indian System of Medicine are legally recognised healthcare professionals and are entitled to the rights, protections and professional respect accorded to them under the law.The NCISM's stand is also consistent with the Centre's responses in Parliament, where the Ministry of AYUSH has repeatedly distinguished between unrecognised persons posing as AYUSH practitioners, who are liable for penal action under the law, and duly qualified and registered practitioners recognised under the NCISM Act.
Article Summary: The National Commission for Indian System of Medicine has warned that calling duly registered AYUSH doctors "quacks" or "bogus doctors" has no legal basis. The commission said qualified practitioners holding recognised degrees in Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha and Sowa-Rigpa were being subjected to harassment, defamation and false characterisation.

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Thursday informed the parliamentary standing committee that Bangladesh's request for the extradition of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina is "being examined by the competent authorities" in accordance with applicable laws and established procedures.The disclosure was made in the government's action taken report on the recommendations of the parliamentary standing committee on external affairs, chaired by Congress MP Shashi Tharoor The report, titled "Action Taken by the government on the observations/recommendations contained in the ninth report of the committee on the subject 'Future of India-Bangladesh Relationship'", was tabled in Parliament on Thursday.The committee said it had taken note of the Bangladesh government's extradition request following the pronouncement of a death sentence against Hasina in absentia and urged the Centre to keep it informed about the progress in examining the matter.The committee also noted that Hasina's stay in India is guided by the country's "civilisational ethos and humanitarian tradition of offering refuge to individuals facing circumstances of grave distress or existential threat."It said the government had clarified that Hasina has not been provided any political platform or space to undertake political activities from Indian territory.According to the panel, India has maintained the principle that its territory will not be used for political activities directed against another country.The committee also recommended that the government continue its "principled and humanitarian approach", while ensuring such situations are handled with due sensitivity and in line with India's international responsibilities.Hasina has been living in India since August 2024 after fleeing Bangladesh following the collapse of the Awami League government amid a massive student-led uprising.Bilateral ties between India and Bangladesh deteriorated after the interim government led by Muhammad Yunus assumed office following Hasina's ouster. A new Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) government headed by PM Tarique Rahman took office after the February 2026 parliamentary elections.
Article Summary: The Centre informed the parliamentary standing committee that Bangladesh's request for the extradition of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina is "being examined" Hasina has been living in India since August 2024 after fleeing Bangladesh following the collapse of the Awami League government amid a massive student-led uprising.

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Thursday sharply challenged the Supreme Court’s observations on the use of pellet guns during student protests. CJP spokesperson Saurav Das accused the court of failing to rigorously examine whether the police action against peaceful demonstrators on July 20 was justified.Responding to the hearing on petitions related to the Delhi protest crackdown, Das said the court’s position raised serious questions about the use of force against non-violent protesters and who authorised it.“The Supreme Court has stated that pellet guns may be used in exceptional circumstances. First, did the peaceful protesters actually create such exceptional circumstances on July 20th?... There was no situation that warranted the use of pellet guns.... The Supreme Court should have rigorously examined whether the circumstances truly justified an action that caused a person to lose their eyesight. The second point is: Can pellet guns be used against peaceful protesters under any circumstances?. .. Ultimately, the Home Minister was responsible for supervision and issuing orders... The Supreme Court, too, needs to give serious and strict consideration to these matters, rather than simply rubber-stamping or endorsing such measures,” Das said.His remarks came after the Supreme Court heard a petition challenging the Delhi Police’s use of pellet guns during the July 20 march from Jantar Mantar to Parliament, during which several protesters were injured, and some allegedly suffered permanent loss of eyesight.The CJP has maintained that the march was peaceful and that the police response was disproportionate.According to the party, police attempted to stop the procession through a lathi charge and the firing of pellet guns. Das sought to place responsibility squarely on the government rather than on procedural justifications for the use of force.“The opposition is doing its job. Its role is precisely to ask questions and hold the government accountable. I saw that a discussion was taking place in Parliament. There ought to be a discussion on who issued the orders on July 20th, and who will answer for the conduct of the police towards the protesters and the brutality inflicted upon them? Naturally, the Home Minister should provide an answer regarding this matter,” he said.The remarks came as the CJP has continued to question the handling of the July 20 protests in both political and legal forums. Earlier, Das had also criticised a separate Supreme Court interim order in a batch of PILs related to the protests, arguing that it could allow governments to continue investigations against protesters despite what he described as the Centre’s assurance that FIRs would be withdrawn.For the CJP, the debate has moved beyond crowd control and entered the realm of public accountability. The party insists that the central question is not simply whether pellet guns can be used in exceptional circumstances, but whether the events of July 20 ever met that threshold in the first place.

NEW DELHI: Will Bihar's Bankipur stand with the BJP , as it has over the years, or will it give Prashant Kishor a victory on debut? Or, will Tejashwi Yadav's RJD will finally have something to cheer about? The fate of the three key contenders in the crucial byelection have been sealed in EVM machines and the people's verdict will be known on August 3, when the votes are counted. So, what made this by-election grab so much of national attention?The Bankipur bypoll was necessitated after Nitin Nabin , who represented the urban Patna seat for nearly two decades, resigned from Bihar assembly to become a member of Rajya Sabha. This followed his elevation as BJP president earlier this year. The Bankipur seat has been a BJP bastion for over three decades with Nitin Nabin's family winning from the constituency for over 35 years. Before Nitin Nabin, the constituency was represented by his father Nabin Kishore Prasad Sinha. And that explains why winning today's election is so important for the BJP.But what could have been a cakewalk for BJP and its chief Nitin Nabin was turned into a formidable challenge with the entry of election strategist turned politician Prashant Kishor in the election arena. Kishor's entry made today's election a three-cornered contest.For Prashant Kishor, whose party Jan Suraj was outrightly rejected by the people of the state in the assembly elections last year, this bypoll is a litmus test. Kishor, who has scripted success stories of several parties and leaders as an election-strategist, would hope that the people of Bankipur would give his political career a much-needed boost.And finally the RJD, the third pole of this electoral battle, would desperately hope that the people of Bankipur would have voted today for a change. The RJD, which was literally decimated by the ruling NDA in the 2025 assembly elections, will be keen to prove a political point.Polling concluded with a voter turnout of 34.16 per cent among the nearly 3.8 lakh eligible electors, with counting of votes scheduled for August 3.As expected, the polling today was marked by allegations and counter allegations. Both Prashant Kishor and RJD candidate Rekha Gupta trained their guns at the BJP. Prashant Kishore alleged that more than 30 of his party workers had been arrested during polling and accused the police administration of acting "completely one-sidedly" to intimidate voters and help the BJP. "In an organised manner, wherever people of Jan Suraaj have set up tables, these people are taking them away. Across entire Bankipur, it's evident that it's not the BJP contesting this bypoll but the police force. People are being intimidated right from the night by going to their homes; some are being arrested," he said.RJD candidate Rekha Gupta accused BJP workers of violating the Model Code of Conduct by allegedly attempting to influence voters at polling stations. “The BJP has hatched a conspiracy. All the polling agents have been given BJP ID cards,” Gupta alleged, while urging the election authorities to take note of the matter," she said.The BJP rubbished these charges and instead accused that Jan Suraaj Party workers were "attempting to cast fraudulent votes" in the Bankipur assembly bypoll and urged the Election Commission to strengthen verification of electors. BJP state general secretary Nitin Abhishek wrote a letter to the returning officer of the assembly, claiming that such practices undermine the fundamental principles of democracy."It has come to our notice that representatives and workers associated with the Jan Suraaj Party are attempting to compromise the integrity of the polling process by attempting to cast fraudulent/fake votes in the Bankipur bypoll," the BJP said in the letter.Bypolls, anywhere in the country, attract little interest. For the NDA, which won 202 out of 243 seats in the assembly elections, the result of one seat should hardly matter.However, this bypoll is the first election after Samrat Choudhary took over the chief ministerial post from Nitish Kumar.The assembly election was fought with the NDA projecting Nitish as its chief ministerial face. However, Nitish resigned from the top post to take up a Rajya Sabha seat, handing over the reins to Choudhary.The Bankipur bypoll offers the first electoral test of public approval for Choudhary as chief minister.Realising the importance of the seat, the BJP left little to chance in Bankipur. The party mobilised an entire roster of NDA ministers, former ministers, MPs and MLAs to campaign for its candidate, Neeraj Kumar Sinha.Former chief minister Nitish Kumar also joined the campaign through a video appeal, urging voters to support the BJP candidate. On the ground, the party kept up a hectic schedule of bike rallies, Adhivakta Samwad, Chikitsa Samwad, roadshows and door-to-door outreach in an effort to consolidate support.Bankipur’s caste composition also makes the bypoll an interesting contest. The constituency has nearly 3.8 lakh voters, with Kayasths and Yadavs together making up around 25 per cent of the electorate.The BJP has traditionally enjoyed strong support among Kayasths. Muslims and Chandravanshis together account for nearly 20 per cent of voters, while Vaishyas, Dalits, Bhumihars, Rajputs, Brahmins, Kurmis and Kushwahas each constitute between 3 per cent and 8 per cent of the electorate.Prashant Kishor’s political gambit, along with developments such as Bharat Tiwari’s encounter and the recent student protests in Patna, has made the bypoll harder for the BJP than the party initially anticipated.The first setback came even before the campaign gathered pace. The BJP’s initial candidate, Abhishek Kumar Sinha, withdrew from the contest after reports emerged that a close family member had been convicted in the fodder scam.The BJP later replaced him with 32-year-old Neeraj Kumar Sinha after the party’s Central Election Committee approved his candidature.Another challenge for the ruling party is the reported resentment among sections of the upper-caste community following the June encounter of Bharat Tiwari.Tiwari was killed during a standoff with the police and Special Task Force personnel on June 17. In the aftermath, chief minister Samrat Choudhary met Tiwari’s family and assured them of a transparent investigation, the preservation of evidence and strict action against those found guilty.The recent student unrest has added another dimension to the campaign. Bankipur is home to several colleges, universities and coaching institutes, making students a significant voting bloc in the constituency.Large student protests over issues such as employment, education and alleged irregularities in competitive examinations have heightened political engagement among young voters.Police action during some of these demonstrations also attracted widespread attention on social media, ensuring that education, jobs and governance remain central themes in the bypoll campaign.Both Kishor and RJD working president Tejashwi Yadav blamed Samrat Choudhary for the action against protesters.The state government, too, was quick to respond. After a Bihar bandh called by Left-wing student unions on July 25, police detained close to 700 protesters, of whom nearly half were let off after they turned out to be minors.While talking to The Times of India, political analyst Kumar Vijay predicted a tough contest on July 30."BJP initially thought this election would be fairly easy. Perhaps that’s why it made a mistake in choosing its candidate. And when the second candidate was chosen, he too appeared to be a potentially weak opponent to Prashant Kishor, despite the constituency having several prominent leaders to choose from," Vijay said."But now BJP is seeing this contest turn tight. That’s why it has fielded 50 star campaigners for a single bypoll. And wherever these leaders have gone to campaign, they have faced opposition. This did not happen earlier," he told TOI.He added that if Prashant Kishor manages to consolidate Muslim, Yadav, women and fringe voters, it could spell trouble for the BJP."It is time for the BJP to reconsider its strategy, way of working and decision-making process," he added.Meanwhile, BJP state vice-president Santosh Pathak asserted that the party would easily win the bypoll. Although he acknowledged resentment among upper-caste voters, he claimed that they would ultimately vote for the BJP on July 30."Prashant Kishor’s entry has only added glamour to the election. Beyond that, there is nothing new about this contest. This time too, we will win by a good margin," Pathak said while talking to The Times of India."There is some resentment among Brahmins and Bhumihars, but they will still vote for the BJP. Bankipur is a backward-oriented seat. The people creating all the buzz are not voters of this assembly constituency," he added.Describing the contest as a “referendum” on the two-month-old BJP-led NDA government in Bihar, Prashant sought to transform what would ordinarily have been a local bypoll into one of the state’s most closely watched electoral battles."The upcoming by-election is going to be a referendum on the working of the two-month-old government of Samrat Choudhary," Prashant had said after announcing his candidature."If the BJP wins, I will have no hesitation in conceding that the saffron party continues to enjoy public support. If we win, it shall be for them to read the writing on the wall," he added.Despite several prominent leaders leaving Jan Suraaj, Kishor remained visible through mohalla meetings, adda baithaks, chai baithaks, padyatras, interactions with intellectuals and Jan Samwad programmes.However, the bypoll is also a test of Kishor’s own political project.A victory would give Jan Suraaj its first electoral breakthrough and help the party carve out political space in Bihar.A defeat, however, would make the road to revival even harder for the party. With no major election scheduled in Bihar before the 2029 Lok Sabha polls, the stakes could hardly be higher.This bypoll carries almost as much weight for the RJD, which put in a lacklustre show in the assembly elections and is now keen to keep its Muslim-Yadav vote bank from eroding. At the same time, Prashant Kishor’s rising profile, even if symbolic for now and confined to a single seat, poses a different kind of threat: the RJD cannot afford to cede its place as the principal challenger to the BJP.That dilemma captures the existential challenge confronting Tejashwi Yadav’s party. Should Jan Suraaj emerge as the leading anti-BJP force in Bankipur, it would inevitably chip away at the RJD’s standing as Bihar’s primary opposition party.The RJD has fielded Rekha Gupta, also known as Rekha Kumari , for the bypoll. She had contested the same seat in the November 2025 assembly polls, where she secured close to 47,000 votes.An opinion poll by VoteVibe suggests that the BJP retains the upper hand in Bankipur, but Prashant Kishor’s entry has transformed what was once seen as a one-sided contest.The survey projects the BJP to secure 44.9 per cent of the vote, comfortably ahead of Jan Suraaj at 33.8 per cent, while the RJD is estimated to finish a distant third with 17.8 per cent.The RJD appears to have suffered the biggest setback. According to the poll, its vote share is projected to decline from 29.8 per cent in the 2025 assembly polls to 17.8 per cent in Bankipur.The Bankipur bypoll has all the makings of a David and Goliath contest, though it is not entirely clear who fits which role. The BJP appears to be the giant. It has held the seat continuously since 1995, is backed by the resources of the ruling government and has deployed 50 star campaigners for a single bypoll.Yet the party enters the contest on the defensive after replacing its initial candidate and grappling with discontent among sections of its traditional upper-caste support base.PK, by contrast, looks like David, a challenger with no seats to his name and a party still finding its feet after last year's washout. But he carries the slingshot of celebrity, momentum from Bihar’s student protests and a campaign built entirely around unseating the giant.

Prashant Kishor's entry made today's election a three-cornered contest. The RJD, which was literally decimated by the ruling NDA in the 2025 assembly elections, will be keen to prove a political point.
